summary: Stewart County, TN tower; one of twelve 80-foot towers the state bought in 1955; listed as standing; build date, owner and visitor access not found.

facts.design: 80-foot steel lookout tower (one of twelve bought by the state in 1955)
facts.status_note: Standing per Tennessee Landforms; no recent source confirms its condition

events.note: On October 7, 1955, the state purchased twelve 80-foot steel lookout towers for approximately $36,000 (as quoted on Forest Lookouts from The News-Democrat); one was to be built at this site

A former worker's blog says they worked at the Division's Stewart and Houston County towers from summer 1975 to summer 1976 and helped paint this tower. Personal account, not checked against state records

notes_for_editor: No build year found. The 1955 purchase comes from a Forest Lookouts page that quotes The News-Democrat; the newspaper itself was not read. The blog account is personal and unverified. The NRHP multiple property form does not list Dover. The Tennessee Stewart State Forest page could not be fetched (connection reset), so the forest link is unchecked. Access, ownership and visibility from public roads are unknown; no access key is recorded. Tennessee Landforms gives 704 ft elevation; the brief's 214.6 m matches. The brief's height (24.4 m) matches the 80-foot figure in the 1955 purchase note.
